proposals.title: Monorepo toolchain and package scaffolding
proposals.why_now: The repository has zero production code. Every downstream deliverable — types, RNG, encoder, ledger, Electron app — requires a compiling TypeScript monorepo with strict configuration, lint gates, and CI before a single line of domain code can be validated. This is the unblocking prerequisite for all FASE-1 work.

acceptance_targets: Money, Quantity, Price, Rate are bigint branded types; constructors throw on non-integer bigint or invalid value
Tick, block index, octave index are number branded types; constructors throw on non-safe-integer or fractional value
div(a, b, mode) is the only division surface; calling arithmetic operators / or ** on branded types is a compile error enforced by lint or type system
rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates) is a pure function with no external state; same arguments always return the same uint64

Property test: rand called with the same arguments 1000 times returns identical values; rand called with coordinates (assetId=0,octave=0,blockIndex=N) and (assetId=0,octave=0,blockIndex=N) are equal; different coordinates produce different outputs at statistical rate
ADR written and merged for the hash function before any implementation is committed
INV-23 property test: a simulated ten-year tick loop with arithmetic operations does not overflow 2^53 on any Tick or counter value
spec_refs: ADR-002 — positional RNG: rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates) -> uint64; no stateful PRNG, no Math.random
ADR-003 — Money/Quantity/Price/Rate as bigint branded types; Tick and internal counters as safe-integer number branded types; constructors reject non-integer and out-of-range values
ADR-004 — every division declares TRUNCATE_TOWARD_ZERO, ROUND_HALF_UP, or ROUND_HALF_EVEN; no implicit division
Section 12 — INV-02: price(asset,t) directly equals price reached tick-by-tick, requires RNG to be positional
Section 12 — INV-12: no identifier depends on external entropy
Section 12 — INV-23: no safe integer exceeds 2^53 in a ten-year replay; property test required
Section 14.4 — packages/core: integer arithmetic, hash, positional RNG, fixed-point, canonical encoder
Section 19 — DEFINIR: hash function must be specified bit-by-bit in ADR before implementation; spec recommends SplitMix64 over FNV-1a accumulator
proposals.title: packages/core — branded integer types, division modes, and positional RNG
proposals.why_now: Every other package depends on the nominal types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick) and on the positional RNG. ADR-002 and ADR-003 are TRAVADO. Implementing them first enforces the invariants at the type level from the start, preventing float contamination and stateful randomness from entering any later package. The hash function DEFINIR must be resolved by ADR before this lands.

acceptance_targets: ADR-009 written and committed before any state hash computation exists anywhere in the codebase
encode(state) is deterministic: same logical state always produces the same byte sequence on any platform
Objects with same keys in different insertion order produce identical bytes
bigint 1n and number 1 produce distinct bytes; the type marker is documented in ADR
encode throws (does not normalize) on undefined, NaN, Infinity, -0
Unordered collections (Set-like) are sorted by normative key comparison before encoding
StateHash is distinct from SaveHash; neither is computed from the same input set
Property test: 1000 randomly constructed state objects round-trip through encode with stable output; no two distinct states with different logical content produce the same encoding in the test corpus
encodingVersion is a parameter that changes the output bytes when bumped
spec_refs: ADR-009 — CanonicalEncoder: normative UTF-8 byte-order key sorting applied recursively; bigint as signed decimal ASCII without leading zeros; safe integer with distinct type marker so 1n and 1 never collide; undefined/NaN/Infinity/-0 are errors not normalized; ordered vs unordered collection distinction with normative sort; encodingVersion participates in hash

Section 12 — INV-22: two logically equal states produce equal canonical bytes; two logically different states produce different bytes; narrative text does not influence StateHash; finalTick does not participate in StateHash
Section 12 — INV-01: StateHash compared tick-by-tick between live session and replay

ADR-009 — StateHash inputs: ledger balances, open positions, pending orders, allocated margin, currentTick, mission state, NPC trust, player net worth, tick ledger entries — not finalTick, not narrative text
ADR-009 — SaveHash inputs: masterSeed, full action log, finalTick, specVersion, rulesetVersion, encodingVersion
proposals.title: packages/core — CanonicalEncoder per ADR-009
proposals.why_now: The spec requires ADR-009 written and the encoder implemented before any state hash exists. StateHash and SaveHash are used in INV-01, INV-22, and the CI gate (Section 17 step 5). If any hash is computed before the encoder is specified, the hash surface is undefined and every downstream test is built on sand. This must precede packages/world and packages/domain.

acceptance_targets: ADRs written for octave count, periods, amplitudes, and the fixed-point log-space construction method before any price code is committed
price(assetId, tick) -> Price (bigint branded) with no float, no Math.sin/exp/log/pow — lint enforces this
INV-02 test: price(ORB, 9_000_000) === price reached by looping tick 0..9_000_000 one tick at a time
INV-03 test: two calls to worldPrice with same seed but different action histories produce identical series over 10_000 ticks
INV-02 and INV-03 are property tests, not example tests
Octave parameters live in a versioned config file; changing a parameter requires a version bump detectable by the CI hash audit
No use of Math.sin, Math.cos, Math.exp, Math.log, Math.pow, Math.sqrt anywhere in packages/world — blocked by lint

Section 5.1 — trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are fractal noise by octaves; each octave samples rand at block vertices and interpolates; amplitude decreases per octave; result is O(1) queryable at any tick without state
ADR-003 — no float in domain; transcendental functions (log-space construction) must use fixed-point implementation or linearly interpolated lookup table with platform-identical results
ADR-002 — namespaces market.trend (assetId,octave,blockIndex), market.factor (octave,blockIndex), market.regime (blockIndex)
Section 12 — INV-02: price(asset,t) == price reached by advancing tick-by-tick
Section 12 — INV-03: player actions do not alter worldPrice; two sessions with same seed but different action logs have identical worldPrice series
Section 4 — ORB (blue chip, low volatility) and NEXA (layer-1, medium volatility) as the two initial assets for FASE-1
Section 14.4 — packages/world: price generator, macro events, liquidity, bots

proposals.title: packages/world — price generator with two noise layers and two assets
proposals.why_now: The FASE-1 acceptance criteria requires a price generator with two noise layers and two assets (ORB and one companion asset). This is the first domain deliverable that produces observable output for the minimal UI. It also exercises INV-02 (the most important test per the spec) and validates that the positional RNG from IDEA-002 works correctly under fractal multi-octave construction. Octave count, periods, and amplitudes are DEFINIR items that need ADRs before implementation.

INV-07: rounding residue account balance exactly equals accumulated truncation across 10_000 operations

Market buy and sell produce correct four-entry transactions (BRL out, ORB in, counterparty entries) with causationId referencing the originating action
Save round-trips: save -> load -> replay produces same StateHash at every tick as the original session (INV-01)

proposals.title: packages/domain + application — ledger, market orders, and canonical tick loop
proposals.why_now: The multi-commodity double-entry ledger, spot market orders, and the canonical tick processing order from Section 7 are the remaining core deliverables for FASE-1 acceptance. INV-04 through INV-07 and INV-21 all require the ledger. The canonical tick order is TRAVADO and must be implemented in a single readable location with a test that verifies its sequence. Without this, there is no playable game loop and no basis for the save format.

repository_assessment.current_state: Repository is empty: no production code, no packages, no configuration files, no ADRs. Only git structure, README, benchmark spec mirror, and empty history directories exist. FASE-1 has not been started.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: No monorepo toolchain exists. TypeScript compilation, lint gates, CI pipeline, and package scaffolding must be established before any domain code can be written or validated.

warnings: Several DEFINIR items require ADRs before their dependent implementation can begin and must be treated as blocking for those specific tasks: (1) hash function specification (blocks packages/core RNG — ADR-002 says it must be specified bit-by-bit); (2) octave count, periods, and amplitudes for the price generator (blocks packages/world — must live in a versioned config file per Section 5.1); (3) technical enforcement mechanism for division rounding modes (blocks any economic arithmetic — ADR-004 says calling division without a mode is a compile error or blocking lint error, but the enforcement method is DEFINIR). These are not contradictions; they are expected work items per Section 19, but they must produce ADRs before the implementing agent writes the code that depends on them.

FASE-1 acceptance requires a minimal Electron installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI (Section 14.6, Section 15). This is a hard acceptance criterion, not a nice-to-have. Packaging work involving electron-builder, platform matrix CI, and potential native module ABI issues (noted in Section 14.3 re: better-sqlite3) must be planned within FASE-1, not deferred. The proposals above sequence toolchain first to surface packaging problems early as the spec explicitly requires.

INV-29 (contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, sandbox: true, CSP without unsafe-eval) is a FASE-1 acceptance criterion. Any Electron window created for the minimal installer must satisfy it from the first commit, not be retrofitted later.
